title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
text: Probability Direction (pd) often used decision rule: hypothesis accepted pd exceeds threshold. decision made repeatedly across several hypotheses, global null probability can much lower intended. pd.adjust() addresses problem making explicit prior probability global null. primary input per-test prior π0\pi_0, probability individual effect null. exchangeability expected proportion null effects family. Equivalently, may specify global null, p0 (Pr⁡(H0)\Pr(H_0)), prior probability mm hypotheses null, per-test prior recovered independence: Pr⁡(H0)=π0m,π0=Pr⁡(H0)1/m.\Pr(H_0) = \pi_0^{m}, \qquad \pi_0 = \Pr(H_0)^{1/m}. pd reweighted Bayes’ theorem: pdadj=pd⋅π1pd⋅π1+(1−pd)⋅π0pd_{\text{adj}} = \frac{pd \cdot \pi_1}{pd \cdot \pi_1 + (1 - pd) \cdot \pi_0} prior conservative (π0>π1\pi_0 > \pi_1), adjustment always shrinks pd toward lower bound. function supports two testing modes, can mixed across hypotheses within call: Direction-agnostic (direction = "two.sided"): pd = max⁡(Pr⁡(θ̂>θnull),Pr⁡(θ̂<θnull))\max\big(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null}),\, \Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\big), bounded [0.5,1][0.5, 1] construction; pdadjpd_\text{adj} also floored 0.50.5. Directional (direction = "greater" "less"): pd raw one-sided posterior probability predicted side, [0,1][0, 1]. Values 0.50.5 indicate posterior concentrated opposite predicted direction; adjustment shrink values, reflecting combined weight data conservative prior hypothesis.

title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
code: library(multibayes)  # From a vector of pd values (direction-agnostic) pd_values <- c(H1 = 0.999, H2 = 0.946, H3 = 0.813, H4 = 0.763, H5 = 0.891, H6 = 0.987)  # Specify the per-test null prior pi0 directly (primary interface) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, pi0 = 0.65)  # ...or specify the global null p = Pr(all null); pi0 is then p^(1/m) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, p0 = 0.4)  # Simulate posterior draws Sigma <- matrix(0, nrow = 6, ncol = 6); diag(Sigma) <- 1 mu <- c(1, -0.1, 0.8, 0, 2, 3) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 4000, mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma) colnames(draws) <- c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6")  # From posterior draws (per-test correction only) pd.adjust(draws = draws, p0 = 0.4, null.value = 0)  # Also return the cumulative joint statement (this orders rows by evidence) pd.adjust(draws = draws, p0 = 0.4, null.value = 0, joint = TRUE)  # Mix of directional and agnostic tests with parameter-specific nulls pd.adjust(   draws = draws,   pi0 = 0.4,   null.value = c(0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.5, 0.5),   direction  = c("greater", "two.sided", "greater", "two.sided", "greater", "greater") )

title: Prior-odds adjustment for Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: object class pd_adjust (data.frame dedicated print.pd_adjust method), one row per hypothesis. Columns: pd (values used adjustment), pd.adj (adjusted values), pi0 (per-test null prior \(\pi_0\)), m (number tests). global null \(\Pi_0 = \pi_0^m\) returned: exact independence, reporting alongside per-test results can mislead tests dependent; per-test prior \(\pi_0\) robust quantity (expected proportion nulls exchangeability). joint = TRUE joint_cum column added; order = TRUE rows sorted decreasing pd. direction-agnostic tests, pd pd.adj bounded \([0.5, 1]\); directional tests, \([0, 1]\), values \(0.5\) indicating data (adjustment) favoured opposite direction. draws supplied, output additionally includes median.est (posterior median per parameter), null.value, direction. print method summarises constant quantities (pi0, m) header displays per-test table; columns remain available programmatic access.

title: Prior-odds adjustment for Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: adjustment follows Bayes' theorem. Given per-hypothesis prior \(\pi_0 = \Pi_0^{1/m}\) complement \(\pi_1 = 1 - \pi_0\), adjusted pd : $$    pd_{adj} = \frac{pd \pi_1}{pd \pi_1 + (1-pd)\pi_0} $$ prior conservative (\(\pi_0 > \pi_1\)), adjustment always shrinks pd toward lower bound. Direction-agnostic tests ("two.sided"): pd defined \(\max\!\big(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null}),\, \Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\big)\) bounded \([0.5, 1]\) construction. \(pd_{adj}\) also floored \(0.5\), adjustment produces shrinkage toward \(0.5\). Directional tests ("greater" "less"): pd raw posterior probability mass predicted side, \(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null})\) \(\Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\), defined \([0, 1]\). Values pd \(0.5\) indicate posterior concentrated opposite predicted direction; adjustment shrink values toward \(0\), reflecting combined weight data conservative prior hypothesis. Mixed use directional direction-agnostic tests within call supported: element direction handled independently, prior-odds adjustment applied uniformly across hypotheses regardless directionality. Per-test correction joint statement. default function returns per-test correction (marginal pd adjusted value pd.adj). Setting joint = TRUE additionally returns joint_cum orders rows decreasing pd, joint_cum cumulative joint probability \(k\) strongest claims hold claimed direction. draws supplied joint computed directly draws intersecting per-draw directional events, reflects posterior dependence among parameters; pd supplied running product pd values, valid independence. claimed direction "two.sided" test dominant posterior side, last entry joint_cum joint probability \(m\) claims hold simultaneously.

title: Prior-odds adjustment for Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
code: # From a vector of pd values pd_values <- c(H1 = 0.999, H2 = 0.946, H3 = 0.813, H4 = 0.763, H5 = 0.891, H6 = 0.987) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, p0 = 0.4) #> Warning: some pd.adj have been floored to 0.5. #> Prior-odds adjusted probability of direction #> Tests: 6  | pi0 = 0.8584 #>  #>       pd pd.adj direction #> H1 0.999 0.9940 two.sided #> H2 0.946 0.7430 two.sided #> H3 0.813 0.5000 two.sided #> H4 0.763 0.5000 two.sided #> H5 0.891 0.5742 two.sided #> H6 0.987 0.9261 two.sided  # Equivalent call specifying the per-test prior pi0 directly pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, pi0 = 0.4^(1/6)) #> Warning: some pd.adj have been floored to 0.5. #> Prior-odds adjusted probability of direction #> Tests: 6  | pi0 = 0.8584 #>  #>       pd pd.adj direction #> H1 0.999 0.9940 two.sided #> H2 0.946 0.7430 two.sided #> H3 0.813 0.5000 two.sided #> H4 0.763 0.5000 two.sided #> H5 0.891 0.5742 two.sided #> H6 0.987 0.9261 two.sided  # Simulate draws Sigma <- matrix(0, nrow = 6, ncol = 6); diag(Sigma) <- 1 mu    <- c(1, -0.1, 0.8, 0, 2, 3) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 4000, mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma) colnames(draws) <- c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6")  # Per-test correction only (default) pd.adjust(draws = draws, p0 = 0.4, null.value = 0) #> Warning: some pd.adj have been floored to 0.5. #> Prior-odds adjusted probability of direction #> Tests: 6  | pi0 = 0.8584 #>  #>    median.est null.value     pd pd.adj direction #> H1     0.9602          0 0.8410 0.5000 two.sided #> H2    -0.0793          0 0.5330 0.5000 two.sided #> H3     0.7481          0 0.7708 0.5000 two.sided #> H4    -0.0349          0 0.5118 0.5000 two.sided #> H5     2.0256          0 0.9755 0.8679 two.sided #> H6     2.9828          0 0.9998 0.9985 two.sided  # Also return the cumulative joint statement, ordered by evidence pd.adjust(draws = draws, p0 = 0.4, null.value = 0, order = TRUE, joint = TRUE) #> Warning: some pd.adj have been floored to 0.5. #> Prior-odds adjusted probability of direction #> Tests: 6  | pi0 = 0.8584 #>  #>    median.est null.value     pd pd.adj direction joint_cum #> H6     2.9828          0 0.9998 0.9985 two.sided    0.9998 #> H5     2.0256          0 0.9755 0.8679 two.sided    0.9752 #> H1     0.9602          0 0.8410 0.5000 two.sided    0.8202 #> H3     0.7481          0 0.7708 0.5000 two.sided    0.6328 #> H2    -0.0793          0 0.5330 0.5000 two.sided    0.3405 #> H4    -0.0349          0 0.5118 0.5000 two.sided    0.1663 #>  #> joint_cum: cumulative joint Pr(first k claims hold), in the order shown.  # Mix of directional and agnostic tests with parameter-specific nulls pd.adjust(draws = draws, p0 = 0.2, null.value = c(0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.5, 0.5),           direction = c("greater", "two.sided", "greater",           "two.sided", "greater", "greater")) #> Warning: some pd.adj have been floored to 0.5. #> Prior-odds adjusted probability of direction #> Tests: 6  | pi0 = 0.7647 #>  #>    median.est null.value     pd pd.adj direction #> H1     0.9602        0.2 0.7832 0.5265   greater #> H2    -0.0793        0.0 0.5330 0.5000 two.sided #> H3     0.7481        0.2 0.7035 0.4220   greater #> H4    -0.0349        0.0 0.5118 0.5000 two.sided #> H5     2.0256        0.5 0.9368 0.8200   greater #> H6     2.9828        0.5 0.9958 0.9863   greater
